title: What If Antarctica's Doomsday Glacier Collapsed?

scenes.text: What if Antarctica's Doomsday Glacier collapsed? It's the size of Florida.
Thwaites already loses about 50 billion tons of ice a year, and drives roughly 4 percent of sea level rise.
If it collapsed, oceans would rise about 65 centimeters, over two feet, across roughly a century.
It also props up its neighbors. Lose them too, and the extra rise could reach about three meters.
The whole West Antarctic ice sheet holds enough ice to raise seas about 3.3 meters, nearly 11 feet.
That's why it's called the Doomsday Glacier, though a fall would unfold over a century or more.
